lede: Three brackets multiplied together is two brackets multiplied together, twice. Expand any pair, collect, then multiply the quadratic you are left with by the bracket still waiting. Six products come out of that second step, and counting them is how you know none has gone missing.
can: Expand a pair of brackets, then multiply that quadratic by the third.
Count six products, and collect them in descending powers.
Write both ends first, keep a reversed bracket, bracket a subtraction.

md: A product of three things can be grouped any way you like: $abc$ is $(ab)c$. So expand any two brackets and collect, which leaves a quadratic times one bracket. Then multiply every term of the quadratic by every term of that bracket, and collect again in descending powers. Which pair you start with makes no difference to the answer, so pick the simplest.

steps.decision: Any pair will do; expand it and collect first.
The x of the third bracket meets all three terms.
Then the −1 meets all three: six products in all.
Collect like terms, highest power first.

explain: Expand a pair, then multiply by the third, as steps 1 to 3 of See it did: $(x + 2)(x - 3) = x^{2} - x - 6$, and the $x$ and the $4$ of $(x + 4)$ each meet all three terms. $x^{3} - x^{2} - 6x$ used only the $x$; $x^{3} - 24$ kept only the two ends.

twin.explain: $(x - 1)(x + 4) = x^{2} + 3x - 4$; its three terms meet the $x$ and the $2$ of $(x + 2)$: six products, collected. $x^{3} + 3x^{2} - 4x$ used only the $x$; $x^{3} - 8$ kept only the ends.

optionNotes.why: Only the x of the last bracket was used.
Only the two ends were kept.
The quadratic met only the x of the last bracket; the 4 has to meet all three terms as well.
Only the two ends were kept; the middle products are missing.

md: You can write down both ends of the answer before expanding anything. The $x^{3}$ term needs an $x$ from every bracket, so it is the three $x$ terms multiplied. The constant needs a number from every bracket, so it is the three numbers multiplied. If your answer disagrees at either end, a product is missing.

title: Why nothing else reaches either end
md: Every other product takes an $x$ from some brackets and a number from the rest, so its power lies strictly between: $x^{2}$ or $x$. Only the all-$x$ product makes $x^{3}$, and only the all-number product makes the constant.

stem: Write down the $x^{3}$ term and the constant term of $(3x + 2)(x - 5)(2x - 1)$ without expanding.

steps.decision: An x from every bracket: the only way to reach x³.
A number from every bracket: two negatives make the constant positive.
The middle terms need the full expansion; the two ends are the check on it.

prompt: What is the constant term in the expansion of $(x - 1)(x - 6)(x + 4)$?
explain: The constant is the three numbers multiplied, as step 2 of See it did: $(-1) \times (-6) \times 4 = 24$. Two negative numbers leave it positive; an odd number of them would leave it negative.

twin.prompt: What is the coefficient of $x^{3}$ in the expansion of $(3x + 1)(2x - 5)(x + 7)$?
twin.explain: The $x^{3}$ term is the three $x$ terms multiplied: $3x \times 2x \times x = 6x^{3}$, so the coefficient is 6.

md: Three terms times two terms makes six products. The commonest lost mark is a product that never gets written: the quadratic is multiplied by the $x$ term of the last bracket and the number is forgotten. Write the two rows, count six, then collect.

steps.decision: The 3x meets all three terms: three products.
The +1 meets them too: three more, six in all.
Collect: −12x² + x² and −36x − 4x. Check the ends: 3x³ and −12.

title: Expanding Three Brackets
why: The two-at-a-time routine written out at the speed of a hand, beside our own steps above.

prompt: Multiplying $x^{2} + 4x - 7$ by $2x - 3$, how many products do you write before collecting?
explain: Each of the three terms meets each of the two terms, as steps 2 and 3 of See it wrote three products each. Three times two is six. Five means one product was dropped; three means only one term of $2x - 3$ was used.

twin.prompt: Multiplying $x + 5$ by $x - 3$, how many products come before collecting?
twin.explain: Two terms times two terms: the $x$ meets both and the $5$ meets both, $2 \times 2 = 4$. Two keeps only the firsts and the lasts.

optionNotes.why: Two keeps only the firsts and the lasts; each term meets both terms.
Three means one product was dropped.
Five means one product was never written: every term meets both terms.
Three is one row only; the second term of the bracket still has to meet all three.

text: A bracket written the other way round

md: Papers sometimes print a bracket with the number first, such as $(4 - x)$. Keep it exactly as printed: turning it into $(x - 4)$ changes the expression and flips the sign of every term of the answer. The $x^{3}$ term then comes out negative, which is the quick check.

steps.decision: The x meets all three terms.
The −3 meets them too; a minus times a minus is a plus.
Collect. The ends check: (−1)(1)(1) gives −x³, and 4 × 1 × (−3) gives −12.

prompt: Which is $(5 - x)(x + 2)(x - 1)$ expanded and simplified?
explain: Keep $(5 - x)$ as printed, as step 1 of See it kept $(4 - x)$: $(5 - x)(x + 2) = -x^{2} + 3x + 10$, then its three terms meet the $x$ and the $-1$. $x^{3} - 4x^{2} - 7x + 10$ turned the bracket round; $-x^{3} + 3x^{2} + 10x$ used only the $x$.

twin.prompt: Which is $(2 - x)(x + 5)(x + 1)$ expanded and simplified?
twin.explain: As printed, $(2 - x)(x + 5) = -x^{2} - 3x + 10$; its terms meet the $x$ and the $1$. The positive $x^{3}$ answer turned the bracket round; $-x^{3} - 3x^{2} + 10x$ dropped the $1$.

optionNotes.why: The bracket was turned round, flipping every sign.
The 1 of the last bracket was dropped.
The bracket was turned round to (x − 5), which flips every sign of the answer.
Only the x of the last bracket was used; the −1 must meet all three terms.

md: Sometimes a second expansion is taken away from the first. Write what is being subtracted inside a bracket with the minus in front, then remove the bracket on the next line, changing the sign of every term inside it.

title: What Summer 2022 found
md: Summer 2022 Q9(a): most expanded both expressions correctly, then many lost the final mark by not subtracting every term of the quadratic; the report asked for brackets. Some reached the right answer and divided it by 2, which gives a different expression.

steps.decision: Choosing the easy pair first: a difference of two squares.
A squared bracket is the bracket written twice.
What is subtracted goes in a bracket, minus sign in front.
Every sign in the bracket changes, then collect.

prompt: You have expanded a cubic and now have to subtract a quadratic from it. What do you write first?
options: The quadratic inside brackets, with the minus sign in front of the bracket
The quadratic with its first term's sign changed
The two expressions side by side and collect straight away
answer: The quadratic inside brackets, with the minus sign in front of the bracket
explain: The bracket is what lets the minus reach every term, as step 3 of See it wrote it before step 4 changed all three signs. Changing only the first sign, or collecting straight away, loses the other terms' signs, which is how the Summer 2022 final mark went.

twin.prompt: From an expanded cubic you must subtract $(2x - 1)^{2}$. Which line comes next?
twin.explain: $(2x - 1)^{2} = 4x^{2} - 4x + 1$, and all of it is subtracted: bracket it, then every sign changes to $-4x^{2} + 4x - 1$. Changing one sign, or none, leaves terms added that should be taken away.

optionNotes.why: Only the first sign changed; the minus reaches every term.
The square was added, not subtracted.

optionNotes.option: The quadratic with its first term's sign changed
optionNotes.why: The minus must reach every term, and only a bracket carries it that far.

optionNotes.option: The two expressions side by side and collect straight away
optionNotes.why: Collecting straight away is where the signs of the later terms get lost.

md:
Expand any pair, then multiply the quadratic by the third bracket.
Count six products, then collect in descending powers.
Write both ends first: the x terms multiplied, the numbers multiplied.
Keep a reversed bracket as printed, and bracket anything you subtract.

Usually 3 marks, as a part of its own (Summer 2019 Q12(i), Summer 2026 Q5) or as the first step of a longer question (Summer 2022 Q9(a), Summer 2023 Q12(iii)): one mark for a pair expanded, one for the six products, one for the collected cubic. Stuck: write any pair out; the answer is the same whichever you start with.
